references.text: Moses goes up a high mountain, parallel to Jesus taking Peter, James, and John up a high mountain.
Isaiah's prophecy about a servant who would suffer, pointing forward to Jesus' suffering and glory, as the explanation of Jesus' transfiguration suggests.
Micah prophesies about a future kingdom where the Lord will reign from a high mountain, parallel to Jesus' transfiguration on the mountain.
God's voice from heaven at Jesus' baptism, confirming his sonship, parallel to the voice at the transfiguration.
Mark's version of the transfiguration, directly parallel to the event in Matthew.
Luke's description of the transfiguration, which also includes Peter, James, and John on a high mountain.
John describes the Word who became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory - an indirect reference to Jesus' divinity and transfiguration.
Peter refers to the transfiguration on the holy mountain as a testimony to Jesus' power and coming.
